newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end firmer on active trade.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end firmer on active trade.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended firmer in an active session on Friday, with the composite index touching a high for this year of 664.31 points before easing back in late trading, brokers said.

A rise in Telkom -- with an index weighting of 18.2 percent -- to 4,075 rupiah helped the composite index to its 1997 high before it closed at 663.97 points, an increase of 5.27 points, or 0.80 percent, on the day.
Telkom closed at 4,000 rupiah on a volume of 5.8 million shares on profit-taking, brokers said.
Profit-taking in other blue-chips including Bank Negara Indonesia and Semen Gresik also held the index back from a further advance, brokers said.
Gainers led losers by 68 to 48, with 60 counters unchanged.
Total volume was 235.6 million shares on a turnover of 476.4 billion rupiah. The index gained 6.10 points, one percent, on the week.

"We can see the index sustain a slow upward trend which will continue in the coming week as buying interest is well spread almost across the board," an analyst with a London-based securities house said.
"The role of local and retail investors is getting bigger and it is boosting market activity," she added.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue making gains next Monday with many investors keep an eye on Bank Negara Indonesia and a few blue-chips.
Sustained buying interest in cigarette makers Sampoerna and Gudang Garam also helped the index to inch up, brokers said.
Sampoerna rose 3.11 percent to 14,075 rupiah on a volume of 1.1 million shares, while Gudang Garam rose 3.30 percent to 11,750 rupiah on a volume of 383,000 shares on Friday.
Brokers said both stocks were active due to fresh buying on their fundamentals.
Cement maker Semen Gresik fell 150 rupiah to 7,175 rupiah on a volume of 1.1 million shares on profit-taking after recent gains, brokers said.
Bank Negara Indonesia fell 25 rupiah to 1,400 rupiah and topped the active list with 58.4 million shares changing hands.
"It is technical profit-taking. I still see a potential for Bank Negara Indonesia to make some gains next week before the truth of rumours of the MSCI index are known," a local broker said.
One analyst said, however, that market talk that Morgan Stanley Capital International would include the bank in its index was no longer a big issue which could boost market sentiment on the stock.
"It is only a matter of time before BNI is included in the MSCI index. The question is what it is going to replace," he added.
Bank Negara Indonesia is the bank with the largest market capitalisation on the Jakarta bourse. It was listed last November 25.
